senses.definition: Careful searching to find facts that nobody has written down.
senses.caution: It is light and a little playful. About a colleague it praises effort, but about your own work to a sponsor it can make real analysis sound unimportant.
senses.example: Nobody could tell me which system owned that field, so I spent Tuesday sleuthing it out of the commit history.

cues.text: You spent a day working out which team owns an undocumented field by reading commit history and four-year-old tickets.
You want to credit a colleague who found the cause of a recurring cost spike that nobody had been able to explain.
A director asks how you established that two suppliers on the list are actually the same company.
You finally worked out which neighbour has been leaving flowers in the stairwell.
From photographs and a few names, you pieced together where your grandmother lived before the family moved.

distractors: A funded, staffed team that concentrates a scarce capability in one place.
Permission given once and in advance to cover a whole class of decisions.
To avoid something deliberately and on principle.
The most senior people in a firm, spoken of as one.
Weight and seriousness in how a person carries themselves.
